name: Figure and image
statement: Aristotle's will, the first of the four, contains no books and no school: the stem βιβλί- occurs zero times, and no school, περίπατος or successor is named. It carries images, εἰκόνες, to be finished and set up — Nicanor's, Proxenus's, the brother's as his memorial, "our mother" to Demeter — and moves Pythias's bones, ὥσπερ αὐτὴ προσέταξεν (D.L. V.11–16; record, Q0 via #1580). *Author's reading:* Socrates is "a fully constructed figure. historical without history. like logos becoming flesh" (2026-10-13). The record gives the will's images; the author's reading joins them to the constructed philosophical figure, and the join is the author's: on it the first carrier of the position, before any text, is the figure.

name: Kin and person
statement: Aristotle's will carries guardianship (Ἀντίπατρον ἐπίτροπον … πάντων καὶ διὰ παντός), the daughter's marriage, Herpyllis's provision, manumissions. Theophrastus is named in it twice: among those charged with care (ἐπιμελεῖσθαι Ἀριστομένην, Τίμαρχον, Ἵππαρχον, Διοτέλην, Θεόφραστον, ἐὰν βούληται καὶ ἐνδέχηται αὐτῷ), and as the alternative to Nicanor for the daughter (ἐὰν δὲ βούληται Θεόφραστος εἶναι μετὰ τῆς παιδός, καθάπερ πρὸς Νικάνορα) (record, Q0 via #1580; #1581 §2.2). Both are clauses of kin and person; neither names books or a school.

name: Books to one hand
statement: τὰ δὲ βιβλία πάντα Νηλεῖ (Theophrastus's will, D.L. V.51–57): the books to one person, Neleus (record, Q0 via #1580). Strabo carries them on: Neleus to Scepsis, the heirs, the trench, Apellicon, Sulla, Rome (Strabo XIII.1.54); Plutarch adds Tyrannion and Andronicus, "who drew up the catalogues now in circulation" (*Sulla* 26) (record, Q0 via #1580, #1581).

name: Place held in common
statement: In the next clause the garden, the walk and the houses go to the named friends "who wish to study and philosophize together in them", held "as a sacred thing owned in common", with a prohibition on alienation and private appropriation (τὸν δὲ κῆπον καὶ τὸν περίπατον … ὡς ἂν ἱερὸν κοινῇ κεκτημένοις, μήτ᾽ ἐξαλλοτριοῦσι μήτ᾽ ἐξιδιαζομένου μηδενός). No scholarch is named (record, Q0 via #1580).

name: Named succession
statement: Strato's will names it first: καταλείπω δὲ τὴν μὲν διατριβὴν Λύκωνι (D.L. V.61–64). The office now passes by name (record, Q0 via #1580).

name: The duty to publish
statement: Lycon's will divides the books into the read and the unpublished, and binds the unpublished to publication: τὰ δ᾽ ἀνέκδοτα Καλλίνῳ ὅπως ἐπιμελῶς αὐτὰ ἐκδῷ (D.L. V.69–74) (record, Q0 via #1580).

name: The tradition's narration
statement: Strabo supplies what Aristotle's will does not contain, with one verb at each link: ὁ γοῦν Ἀριστοτέλης τὴν ἑαυτοῦ Θεοφράστῳ παρέδωκεν, ᾧπερ καὶ τὴν σχολὴν ἀπέλιπε … Θεόφραστος δὲ Νηλεῖ παρέδωκεν … τοῖς μετ᾽ αὐτὸν παρέδωκεν (XIII.1.54). The handing-over of the library and the school from Aristotle is the tradition's statement; the will does not hold it (tradition, Q0 via #1581 §4.2).

name: Translation across a gap
statement: A text carried into a language and a time the school could not reach. At the end of the Athenian succession this is the carrier by which, on the author's claim, the locked line was opened (§4.1; HELD).

name: Teaching
statement: The dialectic carried from person to person in instruction (§4.1; HELD).

name: The material movement of history
statement: The dialectic carried by production, labour and class. Marx and Engels's *Manifest* of 1848 states the carriage in one sentence: "Die Waffen, womit die Bourgeoisie den Feudalismus zu Boden geschlagen hat, richten sich jetzt gegen die Bourgeoisie selbst"; the bourgeoisie "hat nicht nur die Waffen geschmiedet, die ihr den Tod bringen; sie hat auch die Männer gezeugt, die diese Waffen führen werden – die modernen Arbeiter, die Proletarier" (*Manifest* 1848, §I; Q0, EA-CORPORA-02/02). The negation is produced by the order itself, and a class carries it. The author's ruling names Marx; the *Manifest* is the joint work of Marx and Engels, and Engels's carriage is open to a reader under §4.4.
